editorNote: Fed decision week is setting the tone across the watchlist: bitcoin sank to a 10-day low as a selloff in Asian AI-linked tech stocks spilled into crypto and rate-hike odds climbed, while gold tested key chart support as the same rising rate expectations and a firm dollar offset steady Chinese physical demand.

stories.headline: Bitcoin falls to 10-day low near $63,000 as Asian tech selloff and Fed rate-hike odds weigh
stories.summary: Bitcoin dropped as much as 3.1% to about $63,495, its lowest level in ten days, as a selloff in Asian AI-linked tech stocks — South Korea's KOSPI slumped more than 10% on fears over unsustainable AI infrastructure spending — spilled into crypto markets, while traders priced in roughly a 38% chance of a surprise Fed rate hike this week, up from 16% a week earlier. Ether bucked the trend, rising 5% to about $1,888, while XRP, Solana, Cardano, and Dogecoin all fell alongside bitcoin.
stories.whyItMatters: The drop shows crypto trading in step with a broader risk-off move in tech equities and rising Fed rate-hike odds, compounded by continued outflows from US spot bitcoin ETFs.

sourceLinks.title: Bitcoin slips to 10-day low near $63k as tech sell-off, Fed uncertainty weigh (Investing.com)

stories.headline: Gold tests $4,021 support as dollar strength and rising Fed rate-hike odds pressure bullion
stories.summary: Spot gold slipped to about $4,046 an ounce, testing the $4,021 support level, as the dollar held near a one-month high and markets priced a 38% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate hike this week, up from 16% a week earlier; easing US-Iran tensions further dented gold's safe-haven appeal. China's gold imports via Hong Kong doubled year-over-year in June and its central bank posted its largest monthly reserve add in over two years, providing some underlying support.
stories.whyItMatters: A stronger dollar and rising rate-hike odds are currently outweighing steady Chinese physical demand, with a break below $4,021 seen opening the way toward $3,964.
